powerModel.assumptions: The retained energy model uses 4.2 peak-sun-hours, a 75% solar yield factor, 50% GEL depth of discharge, about 0.10 kWh/day for the always-on Ekrano GX and a 15 m one-way copper PV run. The use profile is UniFi plus Starlink Mini for 8 hours/day, four to six ordinary USB devices averaging about 15 W each for 4–5 hours, and one 600–1,200 W corded tool during a 2–3 hour work period. Use 3.0 kWh/day as the normal planning budget and about 4.9 kWh/day as the continuous maximum-tool case; actual intermittent tools should fall between them. The 590 W USB figure is simultaneous installed output capacity, not daily energy demand. The 3 × 490 W AIKO-A490-MCE54Mw string is 1,470 W, 104.1 Vmp, 123.3 V Voc at 25°C and about 127.37 V Voc at 10°C. One 4 mm² pair carries 14.13 A Imp / 14.88 A Isc through PV breaker 1 and the installed 40 A combiner breaker to the MPPT, with the PV SPD in shunt. Breaker 2 is disconnected. The 15 m PV run remains a planning assumption, not a field measurement. PV cable loss uses 0.01724 Ω·mm²/m copper resistivity at 20°C and is about 25.82 W / 1.76% over the 30 m loop. Around 24 V the array can supply roughly 60 A through the SmartSolar. Exact 2 AWG / 33.6 mm² cable remains the common high-current size for the SmartSolar battery branch and both battery strings, and it is the largest conductor accepted by the received 120 A DC disconnects. The secondary-services feeder is 8 AWG / 8.37 mm² with M10 rings at the main buses and direct #10 rings at the Blue Sea buses; its 990 W planning ceiling is about 41.3 A at 24 V and 52.2 A at the conservative 19 V floor. 1/0 AWG remains on the aggregate SmartShunt trunk and direct MultiPlus pair. Installation approval has been received for that MultiPlus pair to use the upstream battery-string and SmartSolar breakers without a dedicated branch breaker. The 1,200 W tool is about 67.2 A DC at the conservative 19 V / 94% case; with high-power USB branches off, essential services bring the controlled SmartShunt trunk to about 72.9 A. All installed DC branches at published maximum with the tool could reach about 115.0 A, so the operating rule remains conditional. Set the Ekrano DVCC bank charge-current ceiling to 88 A, equal to Victron's preferred 0.2 C limit for 440 Ah. Tool starting surge, remaining fault-current coordination, received terminals and hot-installation ampacity still require commissioning evidence.

batteryCablePlan.inventoryAllocationStatus: Accepted procurement plan: use retained 1/0 assemblies only for the SmartShunt trunk or MultiPlus pair where received length, M8/M10 lug geometry and conductor markings match. Procure every 2 AWG assembly to the final metric measurement and fabricate the two 8 AWG secondary feeders with M10-to-#10 closed rings. Every declared red/black pair uses the longer member's finished length for both cables. The secondary feeder remains on hold for source coordination, not terminal-size selection; the MultiPlus pair is accepted under the upstream two-string-breaker scheme.
batteryCablePlan.measurementRule: Mock up the received batteries, battery disconnects, controller disconnect, external SmartShunt, main buses, secondary buses and MultiPlus at full size; measure each supported conductor path and verify terminal take-up, service slack, bend radius and lug orientation. For every declared positive/negative pair, specify both finished cables at the longer measured requirement and support the surplus without a tight coil or bend-radius violation. Battery and MultiPlus posts require M8, the SmartShunt and main buses require M10-class rings, the secondary-feeder bus ends require direct #10 rings, and the disconnects and controller use prepared 2 AWG terminal ends. Use only approved terminations; never trim strands or drill lugs.

operatingRules: Top wall rocker: Starlink and UniFi together. Middle rocker: Orion remote H for the cigarette sockets and fast chargers. Bottom rocker: both indoor lights together. The common feed is the shared 10 A breaker.
The four ChargeIT chargers use their own 32 A branch breaker. The middle wall rocker does not switch the ChargeIT chargers.
Use one corded tool at a time, with a nameplate at or below 1,200 W. Fully uncoil and inspect the tool lead. Switch Orion off and open the ChargeIT branch breaker during tool use.
Work mainly in sunny hours. Stop tool loads around 50% state of charge and preserve the remaining battery energy for essential services.
Switch the MultiPlus off when AC power is not required. This does not shut down DC services or isolate the solar panels. Use the top rocker to turn Internet off overnight.
Leave the Ekrano powered for battery history and local alarms. Keep the existing 88 A system charge-current limit for the two-string GEL bank. Never equalize GEL batteries.
PV breaker 2 is disconnected and is not an operating control. The active PV path includes breaker 1 and the combiner breaker. The surge protector is not an on/off switch.

Battery-string cutoffs A and B and the MPPT battery-side cutoff are separate from the everyday wall rockers. Use the installed isolation procedure before maintenance; the simple diagram is a functional guide.
The battery labels are A1, A2, B1 and B2, north to south along the west wall. A1–A2 form string A; B1–B2 form string B.
Keep the equipment dry and inspect for salt, moisture, corrosion and damaged cables. Investigate alarms locally before resetting them.

The reported PV earth chain is mounting rails → PV surge protector → MultiPlus chassis → grounding rod. No separate earth busbar is installed. AC protective earth and neutral are distinct; the exact reported bridge terminals are awaiting clarification.
commissioning: Installed record: hardware is fixed and already on Fulaga. Earlier procurement, enclosure selection and fabrication instructions are retained only in the archived pre-installation record.

Record the exact PE and N markings at both RCBO + SPD assemblies and the generator/outlet earth continuity. The owner reported bridges at each assembly; the diagram retains PE continuity provisionally and does not represent neutral as a substitute for protective earth.
The reported MultiPlus V-sense negative lead terminates at A1 negative. Record the positive voltage-sense terminal and destination, if connected; do not infer a second installed wire.
Confirm the active PV sequence: roof string → PV breaker 1 → 40 A DC 600 V combiner → MPPT, with the DC 600 V 40 kA SPD connected in shunt. PV breaker 2 is present but disconnected.
Record actual enclosure dimensions and cable lengths if measured. The 3D view follows the reported arrangement and partial photo; expanded routing envelopes are illustrative.

Three-gang wall switch: top Internet, middle Orion H, bottom lights. Each rocker has common, on and unused loop terminals. Commons are daisy-chained from the shared 10 A positive feed. Only Internet on returns to the three-way WAGO in the secondary box; Orion H and lights run directly.
Two indoor lights share one two-conductor string with a middle splice. No outdoor light circuit is installed. Cigarette socket negatives return to the Orion common negative.

Retain the recorded electrical ratings and existing operating limits. Installation completion does not supply missing breaker, terminal, fault-current or commissioning measurements; document actual test results when available.
